PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS

JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND
LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR
CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY
EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE
PROJECT

STATEMENT OF CLARE NELSON IN SUPPORT OF JAY BRADLEY'S
MOTION REQUESTING DISCLOSURE AND CONDITIONAL RECUSAL OF
CHAIRMAN THOMAS GLEESON

November 16, 2026

TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:

I am Clare Nelson, an affected landowner in Burnet County, Texas, whose property is impacted
by proposed Segment I1 of the Bell County East to Big Hill 765-kV transmission line project.

I respectfully submit this statement in support of Jay Bradley's motion in PUC Docket No. 59475
requesting disclosure of information concerning a December 16, 2025 closed-door transmission
roundtable involving Chairman Thomas Gleeson and representatives of electric transmission
utilities, and requesting Chairman Gleeson's recusal if the disclosed facts establish grounds for
recusal.

My support is based on the importance of transparency, impartiality, and public confidence in the
Commission's decision-making process.

Basis for Support

On October 27, 2026, POLITICO published an investigative report by Shelby Webb titled “How
Big Tech and Abbott made Texas the ‘epicenter’ of data centers.” The article reported that senior
officials from Governor Abbott's office held a closed-door meeting on December 16, 2025, with
representatives of major technology companies and electric transmission utilities.

According to POLITICO, Governor Abbott's chief of staff, Robert Black, identified the meeting
on his calendar as a “transmission roundtable.” PUCT Chairman Thomas Gleeson was listed
among the confirmed attendees, along with senior ERCOT officials and representatives of
Oncor, AEP Texas, CenterPoint Energy, and Texas-New Mexico Power. Oncor confirmed that
its vice president of regulatory affairs attended. Notably, the Office of Public Utility Counsel was
not represented on the attendee list.
 POLITICO further reported that two days later, on December 18, 2025, ERCOT presented
significant changes to its proposed process for connecting large electricity users, primarily data
centers, to the Texas grid.

These circumstances raise legitimate questions about the nature and substance of the discussions,
particularly because Oncor is an applicant in Docket No. 59475 and has a substantial financial
interest in transmission infrastructure development.

I recognize that meetings between regulators and industry representatives are not inherently
improper. However, when such meetings involve entities with direct interests in pending or
anticipated contested proceedings, transparency regarding the subjects discussed is essential.

Under 16 Texas Administrative Code § 22.3, commissioners are subject to standards governing
impartiality and prohibited ex parte communications. These safeguards help ensure that
contested proceedings are decided fairly and on the appropriate evidentiary record.

I am not alleging that Chairman Gleeson engaged in prohibited communications or demonstrated
actual bias. Rather, I support disclosure of the relevant facts so that the Commission and affected
parties can determine whether the meeting raises concerns under applicable rules.

Importance to Affected Landowners

The proposed 765-kV transmission line will have significant and potentially permanent
consequences for landowners, including the acquisition of property rights through eminent
domain, impacts on property values, and environmental disruption.

Landowners deserve assurance that decisions affecting their property are made through a fair,
transparent, and impartial process.

Public confidence in the Commission requires not only compliance with applicable law but also
meaningful transparency when questions arise concerning communications between regulators
and utilities seeking project approval.

Requested Commission Action

I respectfully support Jay Bradley's request that the Commission:

   1. Disclose the participants, agenda, records, communications, and substantive subjects
      discussed during the December 16, 2025 transmission roundtable, to the extent permitted
      by applicable law.
   2. Determine whether discussions involved issues of law or fact relevant to Docket No.
      59475 or other pending 765-kV transmission proceedings.
   3. Evaluate whether the disclosed circumstances raise concerns under the Commission's
      rules governing impartiality and ex parte communications.
   4. Require Chairman Gleeson's recusal from Docket No. 59475 if the established facts
      demonstrate that recusal is required under applicable law.
 This statement supports Mr. Bradley's motion and its request for transparency and conditional
recusal. It is not an independent motion for recusal.

The Commission's decisions must be based on the evidentiary record, applicable law, and the
public interest. Full and appropriate disclosure of the circumstances surrounding this meeting
will help preserve confidence in the integrity of these proceedings.

Respectfully submitted,

Clare Nelson
Affected Landowner
Burnet County, Texas
PUC Docket No. 59475

117 Impala Lane,
Lampasas, TX 76550
cnelson7@proton.me
